input_evidence_files.discrepancy_with_node_report: FINAL_VERDICT shows rows=0, but node report (from same ckpt data) shows 30 pool_snapshots, 180 quote_snapshots, 150 fee_velocity, 30 liquidity, 42 market_regime, 6 actual_fee_accrual_placeholder. The trap EXIT verdict was written with default zeros, overwriting the in-progress post-6h aggregate block which had populated real values.

input_evidence_files.label: supervisor_script
input_evidence_files.post_6h_block_bug: line 537 has 'LP_LONG_HORIZON_READONLY_COLLECTOR FIX_REPEAT' (space, not underscore) which is a typo that would only trigger if actual_runtime_valid_for_6h_gate=false (it's true at 360 min, so not the trigger). Actual bug is: supervisor's post-6h block (Python heredoc at line 350) must have failed before reaching FINAL_VERDICT.json write, then trap EXIT fired and overwrote with default zeros. Root cause: not yet pinpointed from logs (post-6h block left no Python traceback).

root_cause_analysis.v2_supervisor_behavior: 6h wallclock completed cleanly (T0=04:51:15Z, END_TS=10:51:29Z, real 360 min). 6 checkpoints generated (each 7 files). Supervisor post-6h block (Python heredoc that aggregates row counts + writes 6+ reports + FINAL_VERDICT.json) appears to have failed before FINAL_VERDICT.json write, because the supervisor log shows [trap] EXIT rc=1 immediately after [6h end] but no [finalize] all 6 reports + FINAL_VERDICT written. The fail-safe trap then wrote a FAIL verdict with default-zero row counts, overwriting whatever was about to be written.
root_cause_analysis.node_report_view: Node report generator (`scripts/lp_long_horizon_node_report_generator_v1.py`) ran standalone on the same ckpt data, successfully aggregated 30/180/150/30/42/6 rows, and produced PASS verdict. This proves: 1) data is intact; 2) aggregate logic works; 3) supervisor finalize block is the broken step (not the ckpt generation step).
root_cause_analysis.preserved_invariant: V2's fail-safe trap (V1 'no silent loss' fix) successfully wrote a verdict, so V2's 6h run state is **not** silently lost — it is recorded as FAIL with full timestamp, runtime, and finalize_error. The trap is a feature, not a bug. The bug is that the post-6h block fails before the successful finalize write.

rebuild_decision.rebuild_approach: Build a new standalone Python script `scripts/rebuild_lp_long_horizon_6h_verdict_from_checkpoints_v1.py` that: (1) reads data_dir + source_verdict, (2) re-aggregates row counts from ckpts (using the same dedup logic), (3) computes corrected gate, (4) writes CORRECTED_FINAL_VERDICT.json + 6 supporting reports to a NEW report_dir (reports/lp_long_horizon_6h_finalizer_rebuild/20260605_043726/) — never touching the original V2 FINAL_VERDICT.
rebuild_decision.fix_supervisor_for_future_runs: Separately, also patch scripts/run_lp_long_horizon_readonly_6h_once.sh: (a) line 537 typo (LP_LONG_HORIZON_READONLY_COLLECTOR FIX_REPEAT → LP_LONG_HORIZON_READONLY_COLLECTOR_6H_REAL_WALLCLOCK_FIX_REPEAT); (b) add aggregate-failure handler that writes a CORRECTED_FINAL_VERDICT_FALLBACK.json with the actual error and tries to write the row counts from the aggregate log if available; (c) tighten trap logic: trap should NOT overwrite a successful FINAL_VERDICT (already correct in code at line 102-104, but verify); (d) add a finalize-success marker file so trap can detect success even if FINAL_VERDICT.json was corrupted during write.
rebuild_decision.no_overwrite_original: Original `reports/lp_long_horizon_readonly_collector_6h_run/20260605_043726/FINAL_VERDICT.json` is **read-only** in this stage. Rebuild writes to a new path.
